summary: Wicomico County steel tower raised near Quantico (1931 per newspapers, 1941 per NHLR); moved in 1999 to the Chesapeake Fire Museum in Hebron, where it stands with its top 60 feet restored.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7' x 7' metal cab and a roof walk (the Register calls it a 'widow's walk')
facts.status_note: Standing at the Chesapeake Fire Museum; the original Quantico site is listed as gone. Newspapers give a 100-foot height, which conflicts with the Register's 140 feet
facts.agency: Maryland Forest Service built it (NHLR); the Chesapeake Fire Museum administers it (NHLR)

events.note: Evening Journal, July 16, 1931: a 100-foot tower recently erected at Quantico; The Forest Worker, September 1931: ready for service in July. Conflicts with the Register's 1941 date
NHLR: constructed near Hebron in Wicomico County in 1941 by the Maryland Forest Service; conflicts with the 1931 newspaper dates
Newspaper report of an April 23, 1942 forest fire names towerman Marion Bailey of the Quantico lookout
Moved to the Chesapeake Fire Museum; the top 60 feet and cab were reconstructed and restored

corrections.current: None relocated (Moved from Quantico to the Chesapeake Fire Museum.)
corrections.proposed: relocated 1999 to the Chesapeake Fire Museum, Hebron
corrections.why: The Register and the Forest Lookouts page both date the move to 1999; the record's 'None relocated' contradicts its own note about the move

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers from July and September 1931 describe the tower as erected and ready that year; the Register gives 1941 and a Maryland Forest Service build. Not resolved; the story reports both.
The Register gives 140 feet; the 1931 newspaper item gives 100 feet. Not resolved; facts.height_m uses the Register's figure and the story reports both.

The Register's coordinates (38.362110, -75.692624) match the Forest Lookouts entry for the original Quantico site, which is listed as gone. The record's coordinates (38.41445, -75.67551) match the museum entry, so they are kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief events said 'None relocated' and is corrected to the 1999 move. Build year (1931 vs 1941) and height (100 vs 140 ft) conflict between sources and are unresolved. Museum hours and whether the restored top can be climbed were not verified: the findcityoffice listing gives only an address, and the search did not surface a museum website. Staffing is from the Register ('last staffed in the 1970s') plus one 1942 newspaper mention. Used 6 page reads and 2 searches.
